newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - June 3.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Ford Motor Co is on track to post a record quarterly profit while General Motors Corp and Chrysler Corp are battling sluggish sales and labor unrest.
* Enron Corp is eyeing a joint venture with the Italian utility giant, ENEL, that would include the acquisition of about $3 billion of ENEL's generating assets.
* Manufacturing strength rose in May, a sign that April's slowdown may have been temporary.
* Black male workers are falling behind economically compared to their white counterparts.
* Chrysler Corp said sales of its cars and light trucks dropped close to 17 percent in May.
* ITT Corp is considering bids for some of its top properties under conditions that would bar Hilton Hotels Corp from owning or managing them.
* The U.S. dollar rose against the German mark in the wake of the Socialist victory in France's parliamentary elections.
* The Nasdaq has created a new unit to investigate questionable claims by companies listed on the exchange.
* Seagate Technology Inc issued a grim forecast of its quarterly earnings, saying they will fall below expectations.
* Amoco Corp said it plans to sell some of its U.S. oil and natural gas properties and royalty reserves.
* The U.S. Supreme Court is set to rule on whether copyright holders that sell their products overseas can prevent other companies from reimporting them.
* The Dow Jones industrials average dropped 41.64 points.
* USFreightways Corp will be replacing Conrail Inc on the Dow Jones Transportation index.
* Boston Chicken Inc plans to cut about 23 percent of its headquarters employees and will review its expansion plans for the year.
* A unit of Eastman Kodak Co is expected to form an alliance with Germany's Heidelberger Druckmaschinen, the world's largest maker of printing presses.
* Heard on the Street: The stock-and-bond jugglers known as asset allocators are fleeing the stock market and loading up on bonds.
* Credit Markets: Bonds ended little changed, recovering from late-morning selling on a surging dollar and signs that auto sales weakened last month.
